title: Could ancient armour stop a bullet?
author: Artem Novitckii

public_showcase_excerpt.scope: The author's website serves a short silent preview. The full comparison target comes from the pinned 29.49-second editable source and its documented delivery format, not this excerpt.

comparison_scope: Match topic, intended duration, portrait format and complete narration. Use the runtime planner to create a new shot sequence; do not feed the reference's shot schema into the renderer. The result is a qualitative explanation, not a ballistic simulation.
factual_change: Original narration qualifies the reference's blanket claims about armour and projectiles. Some historical armour was reinforced and proof-tested against contemporary firearms. A successful historical proof test is not a guarantee against every projectile or weapon.

sources.title: Arms and Armor—Common Misconceptions and Frequently Asked Questions
sources.supports: Mail consists of interlinked rings; firearms and plate armour coexisted for centuries; hardening, thickening and added reinforcing pieces were used.

sources.title: Armor as Technology and Art
sources.supports: Plates were shaped to deflect blows; some armour was tested by firing contemporary pistols, leaving proof dents.
